text: They spent the first day preparing with the particular grim thoroughness of people who had, by now, done this enough times to know precisely which precautions actually mattered and which were simply comforting rituals — Long John reinforcing the camp's approaches, Will and Marian working through tactics late into the evening, Edmund, insistent on contributing despite his unfamiliarity with this particular kind of danger, helping wherever his own considerable practical experience actually proved useful.
“You've done this before,” Edmund observed, watching Marian direct the preparations with brisk, practiced authority. “Properly, I mean. Not simply survived it.”
“More times than I'd like to count,” Marian said. “You learn the shape of it, eventually. Doesn't make it comfortable. Simply makes it familiar.”
It was Ferret Tam who arrived late that evening, dismounting before his horse had properly stopped, the particular grim urgency of a man carrying news he badly wished he didn't have to deliver.
“I need everyone to hear this together,” he said, without preamble. “Because I don't like the shape of what I've learned, and I like considerably less that I'm the one who has to say it.”
The camp gathered quickly, the easy rhythm of preparation giving way, all at once, to the particular tense stillness that had become, by now, a familiar prelude to genuinely bad news.

sequence._describe: Ferret Tam delivering grim news to the gathered crew, Robin of Loxby going still with cold fury, Edmund's expression carrying old familiar fear. Warm painterly storybook illustration style, expressive and slightly exaggerated proportions, rich saturated color, soft painterly brushwork, comedic tone. Wide shot, 3:2 landscape aspect ratio, tense evening firelight, grave alarming mood.

text: “Blackwood's not simply marching on the camp,” Tam said, grim. “My contacts inside Nottingham confirm it — her orders are specific. She's to take Edmund alive, if it can be managed, and hold him as leverage. The Sheriff's reasoning, best I can piece together, is that Robin's proven himself considerably harder to properly threaten than most men in his position. But a father, newly found, newly reconciled—” He didn't finish the thought. He didn't need to.
Robin went very still, something cold and fierce settling behind his eyes. “They mean to use him against me.”

“They mean to use exactly the thing that makes you vulnerable,” Marian said, quiet, already working through the shape of the danger with grim, careful precision. “The same thing that's made this entire week so remarkable. They've simply turned it into a weapon.”

Edmund's expression, hearing this, carried something old and familiar and entirely unwelcome — the same particular fear, Robin realized, that had driven his father into years of careful distance in the first place, now returning in exactly the shape he'd once tried so hard to prevent.

“This is precisely what I feared, all those years ago,” Edmund said, quiet. “That my own troubles would become a weapon aimed at the people I loved. I simply never imagined it would be aimed at me instead of you, this time around.”

“It's aimed at both of us,” Robin said, firm. “That's rather the whole point of it. They're not choosing between threatening you or threatening me. They mean to use the connection between us either way it can be turned.”

sequence._describe: Edmund offering to leave and draw danger away, Will Scarlett-Sleeves and Long John Little immediately and fiercely refusing, the crew united against the idea. Warm painterly storybook illustration style, expressive and slightly exaggerated proportions, rich saturated color, soft painterly brushwork, comedic tone. Wide shot, 3:2 landscape aspect ratio, tense firelit evening, fierce protective mood.

text: “Then perhaps I should simply go,” Edmund said, the words costing him something visible to offer. “Ride out before Blackwood arrives, draw whatever pursuit follows me away from the rest of you. If I'm not here to be captured, there's nothing for them to properly use.”

“Absolutely not,” Will said, immediate and fierce, before anyone else could properly respond. “You'd simply be captured somewhere with considerably less protection than you've got standing here with all of us. That's not sacrifice, Edmund. That's simply handing them exactly what they want with extra steps.”
“He's not wrong,” Long John added, gentle but entirely unmovable. “We don't send family off alone to face danger meant for all of us. That's not how this particular family operates.”

“You're family now,” Robin said, quiet, echoing his own words from days before with real, deliberate weight behind them. “That means we face this together, whatever it costs any of us. I've only just gotten you back, Father. I don't intend to lose you again so soon, particularly not to a plan built entirely around exploiting the very thing we've only just managed to properly rebuild.”

Edmund was quiet a long moment, something old and guilty and finally, visibly, moved settling across his weathered features. “I've spent so many years believing distance was the safest thing I could offer the people I loved,” he said. “I find I'm rather out of practice at simply trusting that staying close might actually be the braver, better choice.”
“Then let today be practice,” Thistlewood said, gently, arriving in time to catch the tail end of the exchange. “We've all had rather a lot of that lately, if I'm honest about it.”

sequence._describe: The crew planning together with grim determined resolve, Marian Fletcher laying out defensive strategy, Robin of Loxby watching his father with protective determination. Warm painterly storybook illustration style, expressive and slightly exaggerated proportions, rich saturated color, soft painterly brushwork, comedic tone. text: They spent the remainder of the evening turning fear into something considerably more useful, Marian laying out the shape of a defense built specifically around the actual threat rather than a generic one — Edmund kept close, properly protected, never isolated long enough to become an easy target regardless of how the coming confrontation actually unfolded.

“If they want him,” Marian said, finishing her planning with grim, determined precision, “they'll have to come through all of us to get him. Every single one of us, properly prepared, properly positioned. That's not a fight Blackwood wins easily, whatever fresh caution she's brought to it this time.”
“No,” Robin agreed, watching his father with something fierce and entirely protective settling into his own bearing. “It isn't.”

Edmund, watching the whole camp organize itself around his own safety with a thoroughness he'd clearly never expected to receive from anyone again, found himself struggling, for a long moment, to properly speak past the weight of it.
“I don't know how to properly thank people for this,” he said, finally, quiet. “For choosing to protect me, after everything I failed to properly protect in you.”

“You don't need to thank us,” Robin said. “You simply need to trust us. We've gotten rather good, this past year, at protecting the people who matter to us. I intend for you to be no exception to that, whatever Blackwood's brought against us this time.”

Somewhere beyond the firelight, in the gathering dark, an army was moving toward them with careful, patient purpose — but for the first time since the danger had properly announced itself, the camp facing it felt less like people bracing for disaster, and rather more like a family, fully assembled, preparing to defend exactly what it had only just finished becoming.
